I farm the way I always have: I start from what worked last year, then I adjust a little. On my 6 mu, I will still keep wheat-maize as the main thing, because that is the steady grain money, and I have well water so I am not afraid of a dry spell. But I will leave a smaller piece for cotton, because if cotton price is decent, it still helps the household cash side. I only finished primary school, so I do not make it too fancy. I look at my own land, what the neighbors are doing, and what I can afford. Fertilizer costs real money, but if I cut too much and the yield falls, that hurts more. So I will feed wheat a bit heavier, maize also fairly strong, and cotton a little lighter than grain land but not too light. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put the base fertilizer down, water about 3 times with well water if the year is normal, spray 2 times, and aim for around 500 kg per mu. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same land, 4 mu, because hybrid maize gives steadier ears here, and I will water 2 times and spray 2 times. For cotton, I will keep 2 mu, use improved seed, plough once, water 3 times, spray more times than grain because insects are troublesome, and I will not be stingy with fertilizer, but I will still keep the cost in hand.
